checks.finding: Key terms are concrete and have single interpretations: boundary is constrained to SAFE/UNSAFE/EMERGENCY_AUTO; AC-006 plus Field Definitions define auto_compaction as an optional boolean whose true value upgrades only an otherwise UNSAFE signal to EMERGENCY_AUTO; AC-004/AC-005/AC-015 define the normal SAFE/UNSAFE conditions and AC-006 fixes precedence as EMERGENCY_AUTO > UNSAFE > SAFE; AC-007/AC-016 define first eligible task as document order with Approval: Approved and Status Planned or In Progress. Two implementers would not reasonably build different behavior from these specifications.

No direct conflict found between requirements, acceptance criteria, non-goals, or constraints. AC-006 and AC-015 are complementary: the former upgrades UNSAFE plus auto_compaction=true to EMERGENCY_AUTO, the latter keeps auto_compaction=true in SAFE conditions as SAFE, and the stated precedence resolves ordering.

Material negative and boundary paths have observable acceptance criteria: AC-013 covers absent/read-only .sdd/context/ with soft-fail PreCompact; AC-014 covers corrupt or partially written handoff.json with soft-fail SessionStart; AC-008 covers no handoff; AC-010 covers missing node; AC-015 covers auto-compaction during a SAFE state and AC-006 covers it during an UNSAFE state.

Assumptions are implementation-bounded and do not leave product behavior undecided: documented hook input fields, Node 18+ with graceful absence handling, git-ignored .sdd/context/, and committable reports/context/ are stated as constraints with corresponding AC coverage.

The only governance surface is hook trust, which REQ-008/AC-012 explicitly make observable through documentation of the exact hook path and trust procedure; no workflow approval gate beyond that is implied by these requirements.

The specification supplies deterministic eligibility, boundary classification and precedence, field definitions, edge-case acceptance tests, and explicit write/security boundaries, so implementation-policy review does not need to invent missing product behavior.
Project root has no domain/ directory, so the domain-conformance check does not apply for this feature.
